title: The Worst Trap
text: “Not that Gaelion-chan or the other dragons really know anything about dignity, or what it looks like to be genuinely angry. At most… maybe when they’re trying to talk Jack down?”
Rival’s parent went by Jack these days, apparently.
“There’s no question they’ve continued to expose themselves to unsightly behavior even now. The dragons of this world are all looks and no substance.”
“In the wider world, people generally picture them as these overwhelmingly powerful beings, though.”
Ha! As far as I’m concerned, those things are nothing more than experience points, I say.
“Isn’t it more accurate to say that a dragon, despite supposedly being difficult to deal with, managed to conduct itself without ever losing its temper?”
“I suppose even dragons don’t actually want conflict… it’s good that Gaelion’s settled down.”
“She’s way more mature than Wyndia-chan at this point, honestly—”
“Come to think of it, didn’t Wyndia say something about a rematch soon?”
Ren let out a deep sigh. No doubt Assistant was plotting to take down Rival’s parent yet again.
“From our perspective, Filolials are a far more troublesome existence than dragons.”
“What was that, I say? Do you have some kind of complaint?”
“He’s just stating the root cause of the problem.”
“Ha ha… this world really isn’t the kind of place where you beat the Demon Lord and boom, peace descends upon the land, is it.”
“Depending on the era, apparently it was like that, but there’s definitely a question of what actually happened.”
Oh? Now this rang a bell.
“Apparently there was a time when dragons expanded their power, and a great Filolial-sama took them down or something like that, I say.”
Apparently that came from research into Filolial-sama, or from what Fiancée had heard secondhand through Filo-tan and Sakura-chan about the great Filolial-sama.
“It doesn’t seem like there’s really a problem with monsters expanding their territory too much in general. In Melromarc to begin with, the Shield Hero was apparently counted as a Demon Lord.”
“I suppose that’s just what happens to the enemy nation’s symbol.”
“In the end it just comes down to the subjective view of whoever’s telling the story.”
“Since coming to this world, I’ve heard and seen more than enough to know that actual humans are scarier than monsters.”
Chatting away like that, we pressed onward. Of course, along the way, whenever some topic came up in our idle conversation, we also ended up fighting the likes of Usapil bosses.
“No, I say! I cannot fight here, I say!”
“Guaaah! Gua gua!”
On a certain floor, I stood blocking Father and the others’ path, I say. And it was there that Father tried to restrain me by locking me in a full nelson.
“Naofumi-san! Please make sure you keep a firm hold on Motoyasu-san. Otherwise our lives could be in danger.”
“I know, I know! Motoyasu-kun, calm down!”
Father pinned both my arms and pushed me down, holding me still so I couldn’t move, I say. Do you expect me to sit calmly while this spectacle unfolds before my very eyes!
“How could anyone stay calm at a time like this! Ren! Itsuki! I will not forgive this, I say!”

Yes—the monsters that had appeared this time were Filolial-sama. Perhaps in a foul mood, they lunged at us the moment they laid eyes on us, but I could neither bring myself to fight against Filolial-sama, nor stand by and watch them be attacked, I say. I tried to talk them down, but no one would lend me an ear.
“I really wish Motoyasu-san would understand. It seems that anything other than the monsters actually native to the island are just illusions of some kind.”
“It’s probably just a simple dungeon mechanic, but for us it’s more troublesome than any half-baked instant-death trap.”
“Terribly troublesome. Let’s finish them off in one go!”
“Right!”
And with that, Ren and Itsuki each unleashed their skills, and the Filolial-sama were blown away into nothingness, I say.
“Gyaaaaaaaah! Ren! Itsukiiiiiii!”
I couldn’t reach the falling Filolial-sama in time, I say. And just like that, they vanished like smoke.
“Motoyasu-kun? Calm down, okay? That was an illusion, and we only fought it because we can’t proceed without defeating it, so absolutely no making a scene.”

Father tried to calm me by holding me close, but I had already locked onto Ren and Itsuki, I say. Both Ren and Itsuki braced themselves, ready for whatever attack I might unleash at any moment. I was going to slaughter them, I say!
“The Bloody Usaunie has targeted us.”
“Fanatics really are nothing but trouble, I have to say.”
“Truly. Why does a floor this troublesome even exist?”
“Honestly, I think I can say with confidence that this floor was the single most dangerous one for us so far.”
“Naofumi, keep Motoyasu restrained. Otherwise he’s going to end up killing us at this rate.”
“I know, I know.”
“Sorry about this, Naofumi-san. Let’s get Motoyasu-san calmed down the quick way.”
“Itsuki, if you’ve got some kind of plan— whoa!”
Itsuki shoved Father toward me with a firm push of his foot, bringing our faces close together, I say. Whoa! Father’s face was suddenly right there, terribly close.
“All right… I’ll handle the rest of the adjustments.”
Ren grabbed Father’s head with both hands, trying to press it even closer against my face—
“H-Hold on, what are you two trying to do!?”
“It’s the best move available right now to calm Motoyasu-san down while also making him forget about the whole floor incident!”
“Naofumi, be our sacrifice. You’ve kissed me more times than I can count already, rotten with it by now. Do the same to Motoyasu and calm him down.”
“Don’t turn me into a sacrifice for Motoyasu-kun—! Mmph!?”
Father’s lips pressed softly into my fur with a muffled sound, I say. At that point, frozen by a mixture of rage and confusion, my consciousness simply gave out, I say.
“Ugh… where am I…”
By the time I came to, I found myself lying atop Father’s Float Shield, being transported along. What’s more, I’d been wrapped up round and round in Rope Shield, I say.
“Oh, Motoyasu-kun, you’re awake?”
“Just what in the world is going on here, I say?”
“You got carried away, bouncing around, hit your head, and knocked yourself right out in a bad spot, Motoyasu-san.”
“That’s right. Pretty pathetic for someone who was acting so high and mighty.”
“I have the strangest feeling that Ren and Itsuki committed some unforgivable atrocity on the floor where Filolial-sama appeared, but…”
“…Isn’t that just your imagination?”
“That’s right.”
“Yeah, yeah.”
Hmm… was that really how it went, I say? What a horribly unpleasant dream. Tilting my head slightly, I got up, now free to walk on my own.
“Honestly…”
And so, with Father and the others letting out exasperated sighs, our exploration continued onward.
Along the way like that, we eventually reached a nice round-numbered floor.
“Floor 10 had that boss Cerberus, floor 20 was the Chimera, and floor 30 had that monster lurking in shadows, the Shadow Walker.”
“It didn’t really feel like the bosses matched up with their respective floors.”
“Felt more like the bosses were coordinated with each other somehow.”
“Ah… true enough. I wonder if that’s something they accounted for, or if it’s just our weapons reproducing whatever they’ve recorded in memory.”
“Really though, it’s a relief that with these registered bosses, everyone gets parts they haven’t obtained yet.”
The weapon parts unlocked seemed to be random, but apparently no one but me ended up with duplicates, I say.
“I only ever get duplicates, I say.”
“That’s because you’re looping, Motoyasu-kun.”
Just what exactly was the reasoning behind this dungeon’s design? Truly a mystery, I say.
“Maybe it’s some kind of relief measure so you can get wave-boss weapons even without looping.”
“I imagine if we searched, there’d be monsters of the same name out there somewhere.”
“Plus we can go after the drop items too, so it’s not a bad deal at all.”
And then, right on cue, we hit a dead end, I say. No, to be precise, there was an earthen wall standing right where it counted, of course.
“That’s Motoyasu’s job.”
“I’d say so. Must be some kind of Usaunie gimmick.”
“Dig, dig, I say.”
Digging away with a steady scrape-scrape, I say, occasionally out popped a gemstone or a geode or two.
